paragraphs.source_en: At daybreak the following morning, Mount Odani became the scene of a savage battle. The castle’s fall was now only a matter of time.

paragraphs.source_en: Even on this day, Hisamasa in the Sannō enclosure did not don his battle attire. Whenever another report of defeat arrived, he merely said calmly, “You have done well.” His expression did not change in the least, nor did he once utter the word “surrender.”

paragraphs.source_en: Perhaps human beings can never entirely free themselves from delusion and attachment. Fukujuan’s suicide by disembowelment in truth contained resentment toward Hisamasa and despair at the situation before him, but Hisamasa did not see it that way. Beneath Tsuruwaka-dayū’s blade, Fukujuan’s head dropped lifelessly onto the floor.

paragraphs.source_en: After making certain that Hisamasa was dead, Tsuruwaka-dayū rose with sword in hand and paced several circuits along the corridor. The enemy was already close, and the clash of blades and cries of combat rang ceaselessly in his ears. He had, of course, resolved to die with Hisamasa, but he could not decide whether to charge the intruding enemy and fight to the death or take his own life by disembowelment. Just as Tsuruwaka began his third circuit, a common foot soldier suddenly thrust a spear at him from behind.

paragraphs.source_en: By the time Tsuruwaka’s lifeless body slumped to the ground, the surrounding area had already descended into a chaotic melee.
